title: Memory
description: ADR-0014: host-owned memory. The package proposes, records and recalls; it never accepts or stores. digest is sha256: followed by SHA-256 of UTF-8 text. Proposals use project scope, the execution id as source.run, and model as proposedBy.

id.description: 1–100 Unicode code points, including non-ASCII characters; not UTF-8 bytes or UTF-16 code units.

run.description: 1–100 Unicode code points, including non-ASCII characters; not UTF-8 bytes or UTF-16 code units.

createdAt.description: Calendar-valid RFC3339 date-time, year 0001–9999, seconds 00–59; T and Z may be lowercase.

expiresAt.description: Calendar-valid RFC3339 date-time, year 0001–9999, seconds 00–59; T and Z may be lowercase.

answer.description: memoryFor answers records. For v0.8.0, nonempty bare text normalizes to one accepted project fact record: id legacy-memory, source {run: host, proposedBy: host}, createdAt 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, digest sha256: plus the SHA-256 of its UTF-8 text, no expiresAt. This compatibility record is not persisted. The alias and that record use identical framing, recall rows and memoryBytes accounting: the sum of accepted records’ canonical JSON UTF-8 bytes before framing. Empty text, null or an absent binding supplies nothing. Only accepted, unexpired records reach the prompt; revoked records can update a restored report.
